cond_0001.intro:
We are looking for a Policy Research Associate - Technology to join our team.
This associate will serve as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces. You will also explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers. They will also have a passion for technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
You Are The Ideal Technology Policy Research Associate If
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always excited by the prospect of teaching what you've learned, putting your superior writing skills and excellent oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to ""go above and beyond"" in service to others, you are equally effective working independently or in a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
In This Role, The Technology Policy Research Associate
Synthesizes and analyzes data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Creates high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Extracts key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Explains public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and plans and oversees content production within a defined policy area
Produces content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; transforms member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Plans content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas with the support of senior researchers; engages with members—our clients—to clarify inbound research requests
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
1-3 Years (post-undergraduate) experience conducting research in a professional setting; an excellent academic record
Excellent data management skills and ability to synthesize quantitative/qualitative research, distilling large amounts of information into concise bullets, charts, and graphics
Outstanding time management and judgment demonstrated proficiency in managing competing project priorities and adhering to timelines
Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity
Preferred Requirements
Experience analyzing and visualizing data, proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and experience with mapping and/or visualization software
Entrepreneurial spirit; track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution
Creative thinking and resourcefulness in problem-solving
Active contributor to a diverse and inclusive workplace
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0001.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.

This associate will serve as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces, regularly connecting with colleagues and clients to clarify needs and share findings. You will also explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers, and will feel comfortable communicating those findings to others. They will also have a genuine interest in technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights directly with the team.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
cond_0105.responsibilities:
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always ready to share what you've learned with colleagues and clients, putting your writing skills and oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to go above and beyond in service to others; you are equally effective working independently or as part of a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
In this role, the Technology Policy Research Associate:
Synthesizes and analyzes data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Creates high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Extracts key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Explains public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and plans and oversees content production within a defined policy area
Produces content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; transforms member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Plans content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas with the support of senior researchers; actively engages with members—our clients—daily to clarify inbound research requests and walk them through findings
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.

1-3 Years (post-undergraduate) experience conducting research in a professional setting; an excellent academic record
Excellent data management skills and ability to synthesize quantitative/qualitative research, distilling large amounts of information into concise bullets, charts, and graphics
Experience analyzing and visualizing data, proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and experience with mapping and/or visualization software is a plus
Outstanding time management and judgment demonstrated proficiency in managing competing project priorities and adhering to timelines
Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Entrepreneurial spirit; track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution
Creative thinking and resourcefulness in problem-solving
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity
Active contributor to a diverse and inclusive workplace

This associate will serve as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces. You will also explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers. They will also have a passion for technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights. Most people become stronger in this kind of policy research work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
cond_0185.responsibilities:
You Are The Ideal Technology Policy Research Associate If
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always excited by the prospect of teaching what you've learned, putting your superior writing skills and excellent oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to ""go above and beyond"" in service to others, you are equally effective working independently or in a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
In This Role, The Technology Policy Research Associate
Synthesizes and analyzes data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Creates high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Extracts key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Explains public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and plans and oversees content production within a defined policy area
Produces content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; transforms member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Plans content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas with the support of senior researchers; engages with members—our clients—to clarify inbound research requests
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.
cond_0185.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
1-3 Years (post-undergraduate) experience conducting research in a professional setting; an excellent academic record
Excellent data management skills and ability to synthesize quantitative/qualitative research, distilling large amounts of information into concise bullets, charts, and graphics
Outstanding time management and judgment demonstrated proficiency in managing competing project priorities and adhering to timelines
Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity
Active contributor to a diverse and inclusive workplace
Preferred Requirements
Experience analyzing and visualizing data, proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and experience with mapping and/or visualization software
Entrepreneurial spirit; track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution
Creative thinking and resourcefulness in problem-solving
cond_0185.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0185.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.

cond_0221.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Presentation Center is hiring a Policy Research Associate - Technology to join our team of experts producing insight and intelligence on how Washington works.
This associate will serve as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces. You will also explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers. They will also have a passion for technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights. Most people become stronger in this kind of policy research work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
cond_0221.responsibilities:
You Are The Ideal Technology Policy Research Associate If
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always excited by the prospect of teaching what you've learned, putting your superior writing skills and excellent oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to ""go above and beyond"" in service to others, you are equally effective working independently or in a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
In This Role, The Technology Policy Research Associate
Synthesizes and analyzes data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Creates high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Extracts key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Explains public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and plans and oversees content production within a defined policy area
Produces content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; transforms member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Plans content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas with the support of senior researchers; engages with members—our clients—to clarify inbound research requests

Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity

cond_0234.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Presentation Center is looking to work with a Policy Research Associate - Technology to join our team of experts producing insight and intelligence on how Washington works.
This associate will collaborate as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces. You will also work alongside colleagues to explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers, contributing to a shared body of work. They will also have a strong interest in technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
You Are The Ideal Technology Policy Research Associate If
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always excited by the prospect of teaching what you've learned, putting your superior writing skills and excellent oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to ""go above and beyond"" in service to others, you are equally effective working independently or in a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
cond_0234.responsibilities:
Collaborates with the team to synthesize and analyze data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Coordinates with colleagues to create high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Works with senior researchers to extract key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Helps explain public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and coordinates content production within a defined policy area
Contributes content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; works alongside the team to transform member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Coordinates content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas together with senior researchers; engages with members—our clients—to clarify inbound research requests
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.

1-3 Years (post-undergraduate) experience conducting research in a professional setting; an excellent academic record
Excellent data management skills and ability to synthesize quantitative/qualitative research, distilling large amounts of information into concise bullets, charts, and graphics
Experience analyzing and visualizing data, proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and experience with mapping and/or visualization software is a plus
Outstanding time management and judgment demonstrated proficiency in managing competing project priorities and adhering to timelines
Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Entrepreneurial spirit; track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution
Creative thinking and resourcefulness in problem-solving

Active contributor to a diverse and inclusive workplace

[Company name masked]'s Presentation Center is hiring a Policy Research Associate - Technology to join our team of experts producing insight and intelligence on how Washington works.
This associate will serve as the go-to person for research on the technology industry and related spaces. You will also explore other policy areas, such as research on elections, courts, and Congress. The right person for this position will be able to effectively research, summarize, and visualize information about policy and policymakers. They will also have a passion for technology policy.
This role will be part of [Company name masked]'s two-year associate program. This program's curriculum is intended to give all of our associates the benefit of comprehensive training plus real-world experience in analysis, research methods, and approach to insight-led reporting. The training will range from identifying client challenges and synthesizing research findings to visualizing data and communicating insights. Most people become stronger in this kind of policy research work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
What is [Company name masked]'s Presentation Center?
We analyze, synthesize, and visualize news and information related to policy and politics, publishing content consumed by a broad audience but primarily tailored for senior public policy practitioners, government affairs leaders, and PAC managers. Our diverse membership includes policymakers and senior professionals from the world's leading companies, nonprofits, and associations.
Each week, we publish hundreds of slides, curating and translating complex policy information and political analysis into easy-to-edit slides and charts. Using this background and our expertise, we create custom content tailored to members' needs, delivering 40-60 bespoke deliverables a week.
cond_0563.responsibilities:
You Are The Ideal Technology Policy Research Associate If
You are excited by all types of research—both quantitative and qualitative—and apply a high level of rigor and strong data hygiene practices to all phases of the work
You have prior experience, or interest, in technology policy research
You ""nerd out"" when presented with data outputs, and you creatively apply tools to uncover critical (and unexpected) trends in data
You know when to shift gears, when to dive deep into data exploration, and when to distill the information gathered to produce actionable insight, keeping to project deadlines
You know that research must be made accessible to be consumed and are skilled at producing graphically-oriented research summaries
You are always excited by the prospect of teaching what you've learned, putting your superior writing skills and excellent oral communication skills to good use
You listen and quickly adapt when requirements change, exhibiting a willingness to ""go above and beyond"" in service to others, you are equally effective working independently or in a team
You are skilled at identifying the appropriate way to present given complex material based on the intended message, context, and audience
You are a ""policy wonk,"" and while you may be deep on one topic, you are conversant and knowledgeable across several topic areas
In This Role, The Technology Policy Research Associate
Synthesizes and analyzes data, contextualizing and interpreting research findings within larger ideas, topics, and trends
Creates high-quality presentations based on primary (quantitative and qualitative) data sources and secondary news sources
Extracts key insights for an executive audience, conveying them in clear, concise written and visual summaries, employing data-driven charts, maps and graphics where appropriate
Explains public policy issues for a non-[Location masked] audience, develops expertise in a particular policy area, like infrastructure, trade, health care, or the federal budget, and plans and oversees content production within a defined policy area
Produces content for publication in ""white label"" slides and decks, published through newsletters and on the website; transforms member-provided public policy messaging in a creative, useful, and insightful manner
Plans content pushes, refines and shapes findings and ideas with the support of senior researchers; engages with members—our clients—to clarify inbound research requests
To perform this job successfully, each essential competency and responsibility must be performed satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform essential functions. Other duties may be assigned to meet organizational goals.

Excellent data management skills and ability to synthesize quantitative/qualitative research, distilling large amounts of information into concise bullets, charts, and graphics
Outstanding time management and judgment demonstrated proficiency in managing competing project priorities and adhering to timelines
Demonstrated interest in public policy and politics and outstanding client-service ethic
Prodigious work ethic and spirit of generosity
Active contributor to a diverse and inclusive workplace
Preferred Requirements
Experience analyzing and visualizing data, proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and experience with mapping and/or visualization software
Entrepreneurial spirit; track record of building new initiatives from conception to execution
